content:
Maya: Heads up — seeing a small but steady uptick in client TLS failures from eu-edge since ~09:23 UTC. I traced it to failed KMS unwraps in the keystore path for services using cert-store:keystore-eu.

Maya: Sample log snippet:```
2026-03-21T09:23:41Z ERROR cert-proxy eu-edge-12 UnwrapError key=keystore-eu request_id=abc123 KMSError=AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::111222333:assumed-role/rotator-service is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111222333:key/xxxxxxxx
2026-03-21T09:23:41Z WARN  cert-proxy PrefixCache miss for cert=svc-payment
```

Maya: Two quick asks: (1) anyone recently tightened RBAC on the rotator/keystore principal? (2) can we confirm whether the intermediate cert was lost from the keystore (I saw a shorter chain in the proxy dump). :eyes:

Liam: I pushed an authz PR to tighten rotator roles last night (small scope change). I didn't expect it to remove kms:Decrypt but lemme check the diff.

AJ: @Maya fyi I deployed a rotator tweak yesterday that changed the role-assume boundary. Might be related — it swapped from role:rotator-service-full -> role:rotator-service-limited.

Liam: Confirmed: policy change removed explicit kms:Decrypt on the keystore key resource and only left kms:Describe and ListAliases. My bad.

Maya: OK that explains AccessDenied. Two angles: revert policy or add a targeted grant for the rotator principal. Which is safer for now? We want minimal blast radius.

tara: From an audit perspective, we should capture CloudTrail events for all kms:Decrypt Deny entries and attach them to the ticket before we change policy. Quick grep:```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2026-03-21T09:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-21T09:40:00Z | jq '.Events[] | {time: .EventTime, user: .Username, resources: .Resources}'
```

auditbot: Found 8 Deny events for keystore-eu key between 2026-03-21T09:22:30Z and 2026-03-21T09:24:10Z. Correlating with request_ids: [abc123, def456, ghi789]. Link: https://logs.internal/cloudtrail/1765432780

Maya: Good. We'll snapshot those. For immediate mitigation: suggestion A) add back kms:Decrypt to the role (fast), B) rotate rotator to use a proxy service principal (medium), C) point cert-proxy to a read-only fallback keystore that already has unwrapped certs (low-risk, temporary). Thoughts?

AJ: I can push a targeted grant for rotator-service-limited@role that allows kms:Decrypt for the single key. I will scope by resource ARN and set a 1-hour expiry on the grant via IAM session tagging (short-lived). That should restore traffic quickly while we plan a safer long-term fix.

sre-oncall: +1 to the temporary grant, but we need telemetry: add a trace tag to the rotator workflow so we can measure any retry storms. Also, add a per-route rate limit on cert-proxy for eu-edge to avoid client cascades.

Liam: I'll open the policy rollback PR and include the grant as a hotfix. Patch snippet I plan to apply:```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111222333:key/xxxxxxxx",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:sts::111222333:assumed-role/rotator-service-limited"}
}
```

Maya: Please also verify cert chain lengths after the hotfix. The proxy dump I attached earlier had only the leaf + root (missing intermediate). If the rotator couldn't unwrap, the proxy might have returned a trimmed chain. Check `openssl s_client -connect <eu-edge-host>:443 -showcerts` or our internal proxy debug `/debug/keystore-chain?key=svc-payment`.

ops-runner: Quick check: intermediate is present in keystore backup snapshot from 02:00 UTC. We can re-import if needed but let's try the hotfix first.

tara: For the post-incident audit/questions: we need answers to: why the RBAC change landed without a canary or policy smoke test, whether the rotator service should have a separate service account, and whether our deploy checklist needs an explicit KMS permission validation step. I'll draft the questions.

Maya: Action items:
- AJ to apply temporary kms:Decrypt grant for rotator (targeted, 1h expiry).
- Liam to open rollback PR and coordinate revert if grant not sufficient.
- SRE to throttle cert-proxy eu-edge routes and add trace tag.
- Tara to collect CloudTrail Deny events and start audit checklist.
- Ops to verify keystore chain and re-import intermediate if missing.

AJ: Applying grant now. Will post confirmation and policy ARN.

AJ: Grant applied at 09:28:02Z. KMS logs show successful Decrypts starting 09:28:04Z.

auditbot: CloudTrail shows Decrypt successes resumed at 2026-03-21T09:28:04Z. Events: [jkl012, mno345].

Maya: Can people watch eu-edge latency/handshake failrate for the next 30 minutes and post observations? I'll keep an eye on cert-proxy traces.

Liam: Observed handshake failrate drop to ~0.2% from 5% within 2 minutes of the grant.

sre-oncall: I'm holding the throttle at 80rps for cert-proxy eu-edge and watching for retries. No cascading errors observed so far.

Maya: OK this seems contained. We still need a proper remediation plan (rotate roles, add smoke test, postmortem). Tara, please own the postmortem doc; assign to devex for deploy checklist changes.

tara: Will do. I'll create the postmortem and link the CloudTrail snapshots + PR diffs.

Maya: Thanks all. Marking this thread for follow-up in incidents channel and will add to weekly security review. Closing the emergency work but keeping open for remediation tracking. :white_check_mark:
